payload.text:
The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Its measured gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.

An independent Halvorsen-Pike audit retracted the original 12,000-cycle claim because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The corrected governing cycle-life figure is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold.
